entities.summary: Aldebrandin of Siena was an Italian physician known for his 1256 sanitation guidebook Le Régime du corps. Born in Siena, Italy, during the Late Middle Ages, Aldebrandin's work on public health and hygiene had a lasting impact on medieval urban planning. His guidebook, which emphasized the importance of cleanliness and proper waste management, was widely disseminated throughout Europe and influenced the development of sanitation practices in cities such as Troyes, France. Aldebrandin's work also reflects the growing interest in humanism and the pursuit of knowledge during this period, as he drew on classical Greek and Roman texts to inform his ideas on health and wellness. In addition to his contributions to the field of medicine, Aldebrandin's legacy can also be seen in the establishment of the first medical school in Siena, which was established in his honor. The school, which was founded in the late 13th century, would go on to train generations of physicians and become a center of learning and medical innovation in the region. Aldebrandin's influence can also be seen in the development of modern sanitation practices, as his ideas on waste management and hygiene were adopted by cities and towns across Europe and beyond. As a result, Aldebrandin's work continues to be studied and appreciated by scholars and historians today, who recognize the significant impact he had on the development of public health and urban planning during the Middle Ages.
